articles.title: The Millennials swapping doom-scrolling for gardening
articles.summary: Young people say gardening offers joy, serenity and a sense of community.
articles.body:
When Hannah Matthews lost her father and grandmother in the space of a year, she found comfort in her back garden.

"My mind would be really busy, and I'd suddenly be out here at 7am pulling up weeds," said the 31-year-old.

She is now an enthusiastic gardener, and one of thousands of young people sharing their green-fingered ways on social media.

Hannah, a former English teacher with more than 70,000 followers on Instagram and TikTok, said the gardening community was "booming" and represented a way of "recapturing some space that feels less tense" on social media platforms.

"It brings me joy, and hopefully when someone else is just kind of doom-scrolling, they get a bit of serenity in their day as well," she said.

"I was born in '95, so my generation are the kind of ones who know what it's like to grow up with both analogue life and digital culture," said Hannah, from Newport.

She said hobbies such as cooking, sewing and gardening were her generation's "rejection of this hyper-digital world that feels really all-consuming".

She said it was a "tough time for young people" due to the cost of living, climate change, a "dire" jobs market and AI.

"I'm not saying we've had it harder than all other generations," she said.

"But it is challenging being young and maybe having different expectations to those that our parents and grandparents' generations had, and different opportunities."

Hannah said gardening offered a "safe space" to "take control of your little space of land or your balcony or your pots in the kitchen or whatever you're able to have".

It became that for her, she said, when she experienced the loss of her father and grandmother in 2023.

"I didn't use gardening as a conscious means of therapy but I kind of just found myself out here, pottering around," she said.

"It's cliché but kind of creating and nourishing new life and new growth is just really the circle of life."

Hannah considers gardening to be similar to preparing for a race.

"You'd normally train for a marathon 16 weeks out, which is roughly a season ahead, which is kind of how gardening works as well.

"You're planning joy into your life for the next season to be bountiful."

She acknowledged that owning a house and having access to outdoor space was "a real privilege".

"When I first starting posting I had some comments 'It must be nice, bank of mum and dad' sort of thing.

"I hope to inspire that gardening can kind of be done in whatever space you have - pots on the kitchen window sill, things like that - just the act of making something with your hands and planning it and seeing it flourish is amazing."

Naomi Saunders from Felinheli, Gwynedd, started gardening during lockdown and quickly found herself in possession of more than 300 houseplants.

"I started documenting my houseplants and my veg on Instagram quite early and gardening definitely was not a massive thing then," said Naomi, 32.

She has since gained thousands of followers, and was recently invited to the RHS Chelsea Flower Show to create content.

She thinks young people in particular are drawn to gardening content because they're "more conscious now of putting their phones down".

"It's an online community that really supports each other as well," she added.

"Gardening is something where people genuinely want each other to do well."

For Rachel Griffiths, 37, gardening became a "crutch" in 2020 when the "world was very crazy" due to the pandemic.

The mum-of-two from Church Village, Rhondda Cynon Taf, said she had navigated postnatal depression, anxiety and undiagnosed neurodivergence over the last few years, but gardening had offered her hope.

"I didn't need to make plans with friends, didn't need to try and see people, didn't have to get dressed, have a shower, and make a big deal about going out."

She said when the baby was asleep, she could "pop into the garden for 5 minutes" and have a "little moment" to herself.

She said the garden had also given her family hope during this summer's extreme heat.

"I'm not going to save the world with my garden but maybe if everybody had a little go, then it would help," she said.

"There are so many little things you can do at home which do make a difference."

When Georgia Featherstone, 26, moved to a new area for work, she was initially unsure of how to make new friends and decided to start a gardening club for women.

"The current gardening clubs that are out there are for people with a lot more horticultural experience, more experts, and a lot older," said Georgia.

In the last two months, more than 450 people have since joined her Girlie Gardening Club group chat in order to attend local events in Surrey.

"If you're a millennial, or you're the older part of Gen Z, you're kind of over going out to the pub every weekend," she said.

Georgia is hoping to plan more events in the future, including talks from horticulturalists and floristry lessons.

"With social media, everyone feels connected, but also so disconnected at the same time.

"You can swap knowledge, you can share seeds and cuttings, and that's when you really get the best of the hobby.

"People are looking for community and gardening brings that."

articles.title: Urgent search underway for more than a dozen people after Grand Canyon flash flood
articles.summary: Fifteen people may be missing after a major flash flood tore through Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch in the Grand Canyon on Aug. 29.
articles.body: Fifteen people may be missing or unaccounted for after a major flash flood tore through a remote area of the Grand Canyon, prompting an urgent public plea from the National Park Service. Grand Canyon National Park said 62 people had been evacuated as of Sunday morning from Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area, where significant flooding hit on Aug. 29. Officials are asking for the public’s help to account for approximately 15 people who may have been in the affected area during the flood. "Additional evacuations are planned today," the park said, warning that more thunderstorms and heavy rain are possible Sunday and Monday, raising the threat of further flash flooding, debris flows and rockfall. PARK VISITORS FACE FLOOD DANGER OUT WEST WHILE SEVERE STORMS RIP THROUGH NY, NJ The flooding struck Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Aug. 29, according to the National Park Service, adding that nearly all footbridges spanning Bright Angel Creek were destroyed. Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs said state emergency officials are coordinating with federal and local authorities as the search continues. "My heart is with the families and loved ones of every person unaccounted for after the flash flooding at the Grand Canyon," Hobbs wrote on X. "DEMA is coordinating with NPS and Coconino County Emergency Management to support search and recovery efforts." She also thanked first responders "working to keep our communities safe when disaster strikes." Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes called the flash flooding "devastating" and thanked first responders for searching for those still unaccounted for and evacuating others from the affected area. "The physical damage includes a historic lodge near the bottom of the site and untold environmental upheaval," Fontes said in a statement. "I send my prayers to the community as the search for those unaccounted for continues." Park staff and the Arizona Department of Public Safety are continuing evacuation and response operations as they work to account for people who may have been caught in the affected corridor. Officials are asking anyone with information about hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along Bright Angel Creek that day to contact investigators. The request also applies to anyone with a campground reservation in the affected area. MULTIPLE HIKERS DEAD AMID SCORCHING GRAND CANYON TEMPERATURES The National Park Service said it is trying to identify people who may have been traveling on the North Kaibab Trail between the North Kaibab Trailhead and Phantom Ranch, staying at Bright Angel Campground or traveling through an area known as "the Box" north of Phantom Ranch. The agency did not release details about the people who may be missing or unaccounted for, including whether they were hikers, campers or park visitors with reservations in the area. The American Red Cross is opening a shelter at 8 p.m. at Grand Canyon High School, 100 Boulder St. in Grand Canyon Village, for people impacted by the flooding. Those seeking more information can call 1-800-733-2767. articles.title: Ex-Pentagon official urges US to ‘squeeze’ UK on defense amid Falklands furor
articles.summary: Morgan Murphy says U.S. neutrality on Falkland Islands sovereignty is unchanged but warns Washington may squeeze Britain on NATO defense spending.
articles.body: A report that Washington could use the Falkland Islands to pressure Britain into meeting its NATO defense commitments drew a swift rebuttal Sunday from a former Pentagon official, who insisted the long-standing U.S. neutrality on the islands remains unchanged. Morgan Murphy, a former press secretary in the War Department, told Fox News Digital that while Washington has not altered its position on Falklands sovereignty, he believes the Trump administration may apply heavy diplomatic leverage over London's military budget. "You don’t take the security and skip the bill. That is free-riding," Murphy said, before adding: "Friends tell friends the check is due. Squeeze is accountability." The Falklands' dispute escalated after reports emerged that U.K. Chancellor John Healey is expected to announce that the government will drop its target of spending 3% of gross domestic product on defense by 2030 when he delivers his first budget in October, according to The Financial Times. TOP US ALLY'S DEFENSE CHIEF QUITS, WARNS MILITARY LACKS RESOURCES FOR RISING THREATS The tension comes amid a six-month Pentagon review of U.S. troop deployments in Europe led by Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby, according to Reuters. As Washington pushes European allies and Canada to take greater responsibility for NATO’s conventional defense, the U.S. is expected to retain a supporting role, including its nuclear deterrent, according to The Associated Press. "We can’t ‘withdraw support’ for sovereignty of the Falklands that was never there," Murphy said. "Policy experts know the difference between an unsourced whisper to a British paper that ‘nothing is being ruled out’ and an official word from the White House." Murphy said the U.S. remains neutral on Falkland sovereignty and continues to recognize British administration of the islands. HEGSETH ANNOUNCES 6-MONTH REVIEW OF AMERICAN FORCES IN EUROPE, BLASTS NATO ALLIES FOR PUTTING TROOPS 'AT RISK' Addressing reports from April of an internal Pentagon email suggesting the U.S. could review its position on the islands, Murphy noted the lack of confirmation. "I have not seen that email. The Pentagon did not confirm it. The official word that followed was the same U.S. position we have now: neutral on sovereignty, recognize British administration," Murphy said. "I no longer work at the White House and can’t speak in any way for the administration, but I can say that the islanders voted 99.8% to stay British in 2013," he said of Falkland Islanders, who voted in a referendum that year to remain a British overseas territory. Murphy emphasized that Washington, however, would maintain other diplomatic options without altering the status quo in the Falklands and said the U.S. is actively pressuring Britain on defense obligations. Under current projections, U.K. defense spending would reach 2.7% of GDP by 2030, with the government expected to set a new timeline for reaching 3% on its path toward NATO’s core defense-spending target by 2035. According to the 2025 Hague Summit Declaration, NATO allies agreed to spend 5% of GDP annually on defense and security-related expenditures by 2035, including at least 3.5% on core defense requirements, and to submit annual plans charting a credible path to meet NATO capability targets. AS TRUMP'S NATO GAMBLE PAYS OFF, ENVOY NAMES ALLIES HE'S STILL WATCHING "Last year in The Hague they signed up for 5% by 2035, which won headlines, but Britain still will not lock 3% by 2030," Murphy said. "I’ve watched this town treat a treaty like a suggestion. Friends don’t let allies cheat. So yes, squeeze London on the number." He added: "This is the habit: put a number in a communiqué, then treat it as optional. They signed the pledge. They still slide." Describing potential U.S. pressure on London as "leverage, not abandonment," Murphy said pushing Britain to increase defense spending would be "in the best national security interest of the U.S. and the U.K." "After Wales in 2014, most of Europe missed the 2% guideline while the U.S. shouldered the load as usual," Murphy added. "The United States extends the nuclear umbrella, the intel, the industrial base, the special relationship … You squeeze a budget with tools that move a budget," he said of Washington’s process. STARMER IN 'SEISMIC' CRISIS, UK DEFENSE CHIEF QUITS BEFORE HIGH-STAKES TRUMP NATO SUMMIT "Public pressure from the president. Annual Hague reviews. A dated 3% by 2030, or a funded path to 3.5% core by 2035, before the next UK defense budget. The special relationship is a privilege, not a welfare program. "Tariffs if the White House wants them," Murphy warned. "The UK is playing a central role in NATO and strengthening collective defence across Europe," a U.K. government spokesperson said, according to Sky News. "We are NATO's third-largest cash spender on defence and the only European NATO member to commit our nuclear deterrent to the alliance." articles.title: UK raises detention of British activist with Israeli authorities
articles.summary: Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old student activist, was arrested in the Palestinian village of Umm Al-Kheir.
articles.body:
The UK Foreign Office says it has raised the detention of a British national in the occupied West Bank with Israeli authorities.

Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old student activist, was arrested in Umm Al-Kheir on Saturday after he was forcibly detained by Israeli settlers who had advanced on the Palestinian village.

There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

All settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts are also illegal under Israeli law, although they are often supported by state services and funding.

The confrontation on Saturday took place in a town near Hebron that has been recently surrounded by settlers.

According to other activists who witnessed what happened, Palestinian children were playing football when children from settler families started intervening. They then ran to a house and started to dismantle a fence.

Footage posted online by both settlers and activists and seen by the BBC appears to show Joughin standing by the fence and trying to protect it using his body as a child pushes against him.

Settlers removed Joughin forcefully and took the London-based student to an outpost.

Israeli police said a foreign national was detained by security personnel of a settler community who suspected him of an indecent act against a minor.

In a later statement on Sunday, they said: "The suspect was transferred to the police for questioning, which included, among other things, taking statements that raised suspicion of an assault against a minor.

"Following his questioning, the suspect was taken into custody, and the investigation into the incident remains ongoing."

However, Joughin's family told the BBC he was due to be deported from Israel on Monday.

Activists who were with Joughin at the time deny there was any inappropriate behaviour.

"In every single instance, it was the settler kids who approached Finn," fellow activist Matthew, who declined to give his surname, told the BBC.

The Foreign Office confirmed to the BBC that it was aware of the incident.

"Officials from the British embassy [in] Tel Aviv have raised the case with the Israeli authorities and are seeking further information," a spokesperson said.

Violence over the weekend across several areas of the occupied West Bank even prompted condemnation from Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu who accused settlers of harming Israel's standing in the world. President Isaac Herzog called it the "crossing of a red line".

In addition to the incident at Umm Al-Kheir, dozens of settlers attacked the West Bank village of Qusra on Saturday before the military was called to remove them. Foreign journalists were also injured by masked settlers in an attack in the West Bank town of Jalud.

"The half-million Israelis living peacefully … are most disgusted by a small group of thugs," said US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee who welcomed the Israeli leaders' condemnation.

articles.title: Family sues after 6-year-old girl dies when badminton racket shaft pierces skull
articles.summary: A New Jersey family's wrongful death lawsuit alleges Franklin Sports sold a defective badminton racket that fatally struck 6-year-old Lucy Morgan in Maine.
articles.body: The family of a 6-year-old New Jersey girl who died after a badminton racket came apart and pierced her skull during a Maine vacation is suing the Massachusetts-based maker of the sports equipment. "This case represents a parent’s worst nightmare," Attorney Charles P. Hehmeyer, who is representing the family, said. "The Morgan family was enjoying an idyllic summer vacation here in Maine when they lost Lucy due to what we allege was a dangerous and defective piece of sports equipment." The wrongful death and product-liability lawsuit alleges Franklin Sports sold a defective and unreasonably dangerous badminton racket that failed during normal use and turned its metal shaft into a projectile. Lucy Morgan was vacationing with her parents and siblings in Limerick, Maine, on June 1, 2024, when the tragedy unfolded. COLLEGE GRAD REPORTEDLY DIES IN SIX FLAGS ROLLER COASTER INCIDENT AS FAMILY SUES THEME PARK Maine State Police said Lucy’s 10-year-old brother was playing outside when the aluminum shaft became dislodged from the wooden handle. The shaft struck Lucy in the head and pierced her skull, authorities said. Lucy was taken to Southern Maine Health Care in Sanford before being airlifted to Maine Medical Center in Portland, where she died June 5, 2024, police said. U.S. TRACK STAR SUES PUMA TEAM OVER F1 TEAM-DESIGNED GEAR SHE SAYS CAUSED CAREER-ENDING INJURY According to a copy of the complaint reviewed by WCVB 5, the Franklin badminton set had been supplied at the family’s rental cottage. The lawsuit alleges the racket’s handle and metal shaft were not adequately secured, the adhesive joining the pieces was defective or insufficient, and the design lacked a secondary restraint that could have prevented the metal portion from flying free. The family also alleges Franklin Sports failed to warn consumers about the risk. Hehmeyer told WCVB 5 that the case was not Franklin Sports’ first issue involving a racket separating. He said a child in New York lost an eye when a racket came apart, and alleged the company knew of that case but failed to make a fix. MONTANA BOY KILLED AFTER BEING FLUNG FROM CARNIVAL RIDE OPERATING WITH MISSING RESTRAINTS, LAWSUIT ALLEGES "The company knew that but chose not to correct this with something as simple as a pin in the handle, which would cost pennies," Hehmeyer told the outlet. The lawsuit seeks compensatory and punitive damages, though it does not list a specific dollar figure. The family is seeking funeral expenses, emotional distress damages, loss of comfort, society and companionship, and other relief permitted under Maine law. According to the complaint obtained by PEOPLE, Lucy’s three siblings witnessed the incident and suffered "severe emotional distress." Her parents heard her screaming and ran to her aid, the complaint alleges. HEARTBROKEN FATHERS FIND DIVINE HOPE IN SECRET NOTES LEFT BY GIRLS KILLED IN CAMP MYSTIC FLOOD Lucy’s father, Jesse Morgan, a pastor at Green Pond Bible Chapel in Rockaway, New Jersey, previously wrote that the family had been spending its final full day at a lake cottage when the children decided to play badminton in the front yard. FLORIDA 3-YEAR-OLD DIES AFTER TRAGIC INCIDENT INVOLVING COMMON PLAY TOY AT BABYSITTER'S HOUSE In the days following Lucy’s death, Jesse Morgan shared the faith that sustained his family through their grief. He told Fox News Digital that a friend returned Lucy’s backpack after the family came home from Maine, and inside was the prayer journal she had received about a month before she died. The journal contained drawings, Bible-themed notes and messages about her belief in God, her father said. Jesse Morgan told Fox News Digital he had no doubt Lucy "loved Christ and loved God," and that God welcomed her into heaven. He described discovering the journal as one of the "most beautiful gifts" amid the family’s loss, adding that he believed his daughter had "the faith of a mustard seed." Franklin Sports told Fox News Digital it "extends its deepest sympathies to Lucy Morgan’s family and all those affected by this tragic accident." "Because litigation is pending, we cannot comment on the specific allegations in the lawsuit," the company said. Franklin Sports added that it takes product-safety concerns "very seriously," is committed to product quality and safety, and is reviewing the circumstances surrounding the incident. articles.title: Vote count starts in Guinea-Bissau referendum on strengthening presidency
articles.summary: Ten months after a coup, military leaders say the referendum is designed to stabilise future civilian governments.
articles.body:
Ballot counting is under way in a referendum in Guinea-Bissau that could significantly boost the presidency’s power.

Citizens of the West African nation took to the polls on Sunday to vote on a new constitution that would reform the country’s political system ahead of elections later this year.

Turnout “exceeded” 55 percent and the poll took place “without any incidents that would call into question the credibility of the vote”, Idrissa Djalo, executive secretary of the National Electoral Commission, told a news briefing on Sunday.

The referendum comes less than 10 months after the military seized power in a coup.

The military government says it seeks to stabilise institutions before presidential and parliamentary elections, scheduled for December 6, designed to hand power back to a civilian government.

The new constitution, which citizens were asked to approve on Sunday, would switch Guinea-Bissau’s political system from a parliamentary to a presidential one.

It would abandon the system by which prime ministers came from the parliamentary majority, an approach that has led to uncomfortable power-sharing.

The new system would also allow the head of state to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and members of the government, and to dissolve parliament.

On Sunday, voters answered “yes” or “no” to the question: “Do you agree with the entry into force of the new constitution approved by the National Transitional Council?”

“What we want after this referendum is to allow whoever wins the elections to see out their mandate without hindrance,” military leader and transitional President General Horta Inta-A Na Man said.

Under the transitional charter he upholds, Inta-A Na Man is barred from running in elections.

The referendum follows years of political instability. In the November 2025 presidential election, both candidates declared victory and accused each other of electoral interference. The coup happened one day after.

articles.title: Sibling rivalry: When parents play financial favourites
articles.summary: So-called financial favouritism can cause jealousy and resentment long into adulthood. Here is how experts say you can avoid it
articles.body:
Do your parents have a favourite child and give them more money, gifts or help?

Financial favouritism can cause jealousy and resentment long into adulthood and, in some cases, even spark legal disputes after a parent dies. But experts say there are strategies that can help you avoid it.

John says his parents, who have always supported his younger brother, recently refused to lend him £10,000 towards a house deposit after he broke up with his partner.

This was despite the money being "well within their financial grasp", he says.

His parents had previously given his brother a deposit to buy a home and subsidised his living expenses.

John, 47, whose real name we have changed, says he was viewed as the more academic one growing up and expected to stand on his "own two feet" financially, while his brother, 42, struggled to make his way in the world and was "coddled".

He says the favouritism has made him believe "the needs of others take precedence over my own", leaving him feeling "isolated" and affecting friendships and romantic relationships.

Forums like Mumsnet and Reddit are full of posts complaining about siblings being shown preferential treatment regarding money.

Common gripes include the amount of financial support adult children have received from their parents during their lifetime, the way inheritance is divided , and whether a sibling has supported their parents more than others .

Dr Fenia Christodoulidi, from counselling service Relate, says that disagreements about money between siblings are rarely just about the money itself.

"Financial support from parents often carries a powerful emotional meaning and some siblings tend to interpret differences in support as signs of favouritism, unequal love or a lack of recognition."

She adds that even when parents have "practical reasons" for treating their children differently, failing to communicate these clearly can "leave room for misunderstanding and resentment".

Those reasons might include an adult child needing more support because they earn significantly less, have an illness, or have to pay more to get on the housing ladder due to rising prices .

Ellis, who works in finance in London, tells the BBC that she and her siblings have had "different levels of support at different times" from their parents and it's never been a problem.

But her colleague Tasha, the youngest of seven, says her siblings have fallen out over perceived favouritism, even though she thinks her parents treat them all the same.

"I just think people sometimes get a bit uncertain or jealous and that's quite normal," says the 33-year-old.

"Sometimes people stop talking for a bit or go to process what they are feeling, and they come back together and they just hash it out."

Having "open conversations about expectations and the reasons behind decisions" can help reduce feelings of resentment about money, Christodoulidi says.

"Talking about money is verboten in my family - be it salaries or savings or financial assistance," says John.

"Any time I've tried to air my feelings my parents just become evasive so now I don't bother."

John says he is now planning his financial future on the basis he won't have any inheritance - although he expects to be asked to step in if his parents get ill or lose capacity.

He says he has a "great relationship with his brother" but feels resentment towards his parents for creating the "imbalance" between them.

Claire Webb, a solicitor and mediator at Family Solutions Now, regularly helps siblings who have disputes over inheritance and other money matters.

"One sibling might argue the other was given more money earlier on in life, say, to buy a house, and that the parents said this would be reflected in the will.

"Then the will says, 'everything should be shared equally'. So you have all of that historic feeling of unfairness being dredged up."

To avoid conflict, she says parents need to be clear with their children about what they want while they are still alive.

Siblings who do fall out should consider mediation before taking legal action, she adds. This is when a trained professional helps them remedy their problems.

The good news is, siblings who take the legal route more often than not reach an amicable solution.

"Most of the time there is a deep-down family bond - and if you can crack what started the problem they often find a way through."

Tips for resolving money quarrels between siblings

1. Recognise what's behind the row : It may be about feeling valued or treated fairly, rather than the money itself

2. Avoid making assumptions about a sibling's financial situation or the reasons behind parental decisions

3. Encourage open, respectful conversations where everyone has the opportunity to explain how they feel

4. Parents should communicate their intentions as clearly as possible, particularly if they are supporting children differently for practical reasons

5. Consider family counselling if conversations repeatedly become stuck or emotionally charged

6. Consider mediation before taking legal action in inheritance disputes.

7. Choose powers of attorney carefully: Parents usually appoint their children to oversee their care and finances if they get ill or lose mental capacity. But if there's a risk they'll fall out, they can appoint someone else including a solicitor.

articles.title: Airport chaos erupts after driver suddenly smashes through fence, hits plane and tractor: police
articles.summary: A New Hampshire teen allegedly fled police, crashed through an airport fence and struck a parked plane and tractor before being taken into custody.
articles.body: A New Hampshire airport was allegedly breached Saturday after a teenager fleeing police crashed through a perimeter fence, striking a parked plane and nearby tractor, authorities said. The incident unfolded at Portsmouth International Airport shortly after 8 p.m., New Hampshire State Police (NHSP) said Sunday. The suspect was identified as Wyatt Seely, 17, of Rochester, who officials said was found intoxicated following the crash. According to authorities, the pursuit began when officials were searching for "a vehicle related to reported crimes in other local jurisdictions." FRONTIER JET STRIKES, KILLS PERSON ON DENVER AIRPORT RUNWAY DURING TAKEOFF AFTER SECURITY BREACH A trooper attempted to stop a black 2008 Ford Mustang on Durham Street in Portsmouth. The driver then allegedly fled the scene, NHSP reported. "The Mustang, which did not have its lights on at the time, then crashed through a perimeter fence of the nearby Portsmouth International Airport and traveled across an aircraft parking apron," officials said in a release. The vehicle then struck a Kubota tractor and a small, unoccupied, stationary plane before coming to a stop, NHSP said in a post on X. MAN CLIMBS ONTO US MILITARY AIRCRAFT IN IRELAND, ATTACKS IT WITH HATCHET: REPORT Seely was taken into custody by state troopers and transported to an area hospital for evaluation, police said. No one else was injured. The teen was charged with misdemeanor counts of driving while intoxicated (DWI), aggravated driving while intoxicated, disobeying a police officer and conduct after an accident. He was also charged with a violation-level offense of reckless driving. He is scheduled to be arraigned in Portsmouth District Court on Sept. 9, 2026. articles.standfirst: Não havia outras evidências de que o centro energético iraniano estivesse sob ataque. A Casa Branca e o Departamento de Defesa dos EUA não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentários.
articles.summary: Não havia outras evidências de que o centro energético iraniano estivesse sob ataque. A Casa Branca e o Departamento de Defesa dos EUA não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentários.
articles.body:
Trump fala com a imprensa na Casa Branca após assinar ordem executiva renomeando o Lago Ontário como Lago América — Foto: Evan Vucci/Reuters

O centro energético iraniano da ilha de Kharg está sendo reduzido a escombros, disse o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, neste domingo (30), em uma breve publicação nas redes sociais acompanhada de um vídeo gerado por inteligência artificial.

Não havia outras evidências de que o centro energético iraniano estivesse sob ataque. A Casa Branca e o Departamento de Defesa dos EUA não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentários da Reuters fora do horário comercial normal.

Não houve resposta imediata à publicação de Trump sobre a mídia iraniana.

"A ilha de Kharg está sendo reduzida a escombros!!! Presidente DJT", disse Trump nas redes sociais, mas não deu mais detalhes.

Publicação do presidente dos EUA Donald Trump na rede social Truth Social — Foto: Reprodução/Truth Social

A Reuters confirmou que um vídeo que acompanhava a notícia, mostrando explosões dramáticas, foi provavelmente gerado sinteticamente, usando um software que detecta imagens manipuladas por inteligência artificial.

Atacar Kharg , que era responsável por 90% das exportações de petróleo do Irã antes da guerra iniciada pelos ataques dos EUA e de Israel em 28 de fevereiro, prejudicaria gravemente seu comércio de energia e exerceria enorme pressão sobre sua economia.

O Irã respondeu a um ataque anterior dos EUA contra lançadores de foguetes em sua ilha de Larak, a cerca de 660 km (410 milhas) a leste de Kharg, com um ataque a duas bases americanas na Jordânia, informou a mídia iraniana.

A retomada das hostilidades ocorreu após semanas em que o governo Trump intensificou os esforços para punir Teerã e seus parceiros comerciais com sanções econômicas onerosas, abandonando as opções militares.

O secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, disse à Reuters no domingo que novas sanções secundárias provavelmente serão anunciadas semanalmente, em um esforço para pressionar o Irã, com foco inicial nos bancos.

"Estamos começando pelos bancos e dizendo a eles que não é aceitável ter dinheiro iraniano e ajudar o regime", disse Bessent em entrevista.

Após impor sanções às filiais do Banque Misr do Egito nos Emirados Árabes Unidos na sexta-feira, por supostas ligações financeiras com o Irã, Bessent afirmou que o próximo passo pode ser o corte total do acesso da instituição ao sistema financeiro baseado no dólar.

"Vocês verão muito mais disso a cada semana", disse Bessent à Reuters, antes de uma reunião dos líderes financeiros do G20.

Primeiros ataques militares conhecidos em semanas

Ao descrever os primeiros ataques militares conhecidos dos EUA desde o final de julho , um oficial americano disse que as forças atacaram dois lançadores iranianos na ilha de Larak.

A pequena ilha no Estreito de Ormuz, perto do porto estratégico de Bandar Abbas, tem vista para as rotas de navegação na entrada do Golfo, o que lhe confere um papel fundamental nas tensões com o Irã, na segurança marítima e no fornecimento global de energia.

"Forças da Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica foram observadas se preparando para lançar foguetes com minas marítimas no Estreito de Ormuz", acrescentou a fonte.

Em retaliação, o Irã lançou mísseis balísticos contra a Jordânia, visando duas bases americanas. As forças armadas da Jordânia interceptaram oito mísseis que entraram em seu espaço aéreo, informou a televisão estatal.

A Guarda Revolucionária do Irã afirmou que o ataque matou e feriu vários soldados e civis e prometeu uma "resposta e punição" por parte de Teerã, de acordo com a mídia estatal iraniana.

Em comunicado, o Comando Central dos EUA afirmou ter tomado medidas "limitadas e precisas" contra as forças de minagem da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã, que representavam uma "ameaça iminente" no Estreito de Ormuz. Não foram fornecidos detalhes.

Após os ataques dos EUA, o Irã atacou uma base militar americana na Jordânia, informou um repórter da Fox News no domingo, citando uma fonte americana. Quase todos os mísseis que se aproximavam "foram interceptados até o momento", disse o repórter à emissora X, indicando a falta de impacto significativo.

Em meio às ameaças à navegação, o número de navios mercantes visíveis transitando pelo Estreito de Ormuz caiu para cinco por dia durante o fim de semana, segundo dados do setor.

O número real pode ser maior, já que algumas embarcações desligaram seus sistemas de identificação automática para evitar ataques.

Na semana passada, o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, disse que todas as minas haviam sido detonadas ou removidas das águas internacionais do estreito e que o Irã havia sido avisado de que qualquer embarcação que colocasse novas minas seria destruída.

Embora Trump tenha afirmado repetidamente que o Estreito de Ormuz está aberto, a Marinha da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã classificou essas declarações como "uma mentira óbvia", reiterando que o estreito permanece fechado para navios sem a permissão iraniana.

Antes de ser bloqueada durante os seis meses da guerra com o Irã, a hidrovia transportava quase um quinto das remessas globais de petróleo bruto e gás natural liquefeito.

O Irã é o terceiro maior produtor da Organização dos Países Exportadores de Petróleo.

articles.body:
Ribeirão Preto, SP, é a cidade com a maior população estimada da região — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Um estudo divulgado pelo IBGE (Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística) nesta sexta-feira (28) aponta que as 66 cidades das regiões de Ribeirão Preto (SP) e Franca (SP) somam 2.690.627 de habitantes em 2026 .

O levantamento lista a população estimada de todas as cidades brasileiras.

Em comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado, o ganho populacional na região é de 5.854 novos moradores. Em 2025, eram 2.684.773 habitantes no total.

Ribeirão Preto, Franca, Sertãozinho (SP) e Barretos (SP) são os municípios com maior número de pessoas, de acordo com o estudo. Os números estimados têm como referência o último dia 1° de julho de 2026.

Veja abaixo a população estimada de todas as cidades da área de cobertura do g1 Ribeirão Preto, comparada com os números de 2025.

A tabela está organizada em ordem decrescente, ou seja, a primeira cidade da lista tem o maior número de habitantes e a última cidade, o menor.

Comparativo de habitantes nas cidades da região de Ribeirão Preto

A menor população da região é a de Santa Cruz da Esperança (SP), com 2.173 habitantes. Comparado à estimativa do ano passado, o município ganhou cinco pessoas e teve crescimento de 0,23%.

As outras três cidades com menos de 3 mil habitantes são Cássia dos Coqueiros (SP), Taquaral (SP) e Cândido Rodrigues (SP).

Igreja Matriz, em Santa Cruz da Esperança, SP — Foto: Reprodução/Arquidiocese de Ribeirão Preto

Enquanto a média nacional é de 0,34%, Brodowski (SP), Jardinópolis (SP), Dumont (SP) e Vista Alegre do Alto (SP) cresceram cerca de 0,50% em relação a 2025 .

Apesar da tendência geral de alta, algumas cidades apresentaram leve redução populacional entre 2025 e 2026.

articles.title: 'Killers blocked from early release' and 'Harry should fund security'
articles.summary: Monday's papers are dominated by changes to the government's early release scheme for prisoners in England and Wales.
articles.body:
Several of the front pages feature Prime Minister Andy Burnham's announcement that he will make changes to the early prison release scheme in England and Wales.

The Daily Mirror says the decision to exclude those convicted of manslaughter from the scheme represents "justice for loved ones" and a "relief" for victims' families.

But the Daily Mail believes that releasing some inmates serving indefinite sentences will mean the government allowing "more dangerous criminals" onto the streets.

The Guardian picks up warnings that the plans could trigger further overcrowding in prisons and leave them "one major event from disaster".

The Daily Telegraph highlights a letter from the Governor of the Bank of England Andrew Bailey, saying that there could be a "severe downturn" in the global economy if the "AI bubble bursts". The paper says he has told members of the G20 group of advanced economies that the "soaring levels of debt" used to fund the industry could trigger a "potentially disorderly correction".

The i Paper has spoken to a number of people caught up in a Post Office IT scandal, who call on the prime minister to speed up the process of quashing their criminal convictions and paying compensation. The group of postmasters were convicted using evidence from the faulty Capture system, a predecessor to the Horizon software. They have told the paper that Burnham should take a "fresh look" at the "torturous" processes they've been going through. The government said it is working hard to deliver for them as soon as possible.

Do not trust "unqualified wellness influencers" on social media is the warning from the NHS carried in the Times . It says a study has found nearly half the UK's population is spending more than £120 a year on health supplements promoted online. The NHS has told the paper that the use of products like magnesium for stress, or collagen for anti-ageing, aren't backed by "good evidence".

Pictures of the young sons of one of the two police officers killed in a crash in Middlesbrough last weekend are on several front pages, after they led out Manchester United for their match against Ipswich Town at Old Trafford yesterday. The Sun says they were "united for dad", while the Daily Star hails them as the "bravest boys in Britain".

articles.title: Abbey Gate survivor describes chaos before attack, says pullout was botched from the start
articles.summary: Tyler Vargas-Andrews says Marines were forced to improvise during the Afghanistan evacuation with no tents, food, or support during the withdrawal at Abbey Gate in August, 2021.
articles.body: Abbey Gate bombing survivor retired Marine Sgt. Tyler Vargas-Andrews said Saturday on "The Big Weekend Show" that U.S. Marines were forced to improvise their way through the chaotic evacuation of Afghanistan after inadequate preparation and support left them facing overwhelming crowds in the days leading up to the deadly attack. Vargas-Andrews, who lost his right arm and left leg in the Aug. 26, 2021, suicide bombing, said Marines at Hamid Karzai International Airport were left to adapt on the ground despite warnings from leadership about how dire the evacuation could become. Vargas-Andrews told Fox News that the failures leading to the attack began well before the first explosion and renewed his call for accountability. "Everything we were doing while we were there was like figuring it out on the go," he said, even as he acknowledged that Marines are trained to "adapt, improvise and overcome." ARMY VET LAWMAKER MARKS ABBEY GATE ANNIVERSARY WITH BLISTERING MESSAGE FOR BIDEN-HARRIS: 'ABJECT FAILURE' "We were lacking in the support. We were giving [the refugees] our food. We were giving them our water. There was no tent set up to process refugees," Vargas-Andrews said. He recounted that day, comparing it to something out of the movie "World War Z," saying, "It was just hundreds of thousands of people. And if I filled up the whole room with sand, that's how many people it felt like [were] there." AMERICA’S PROMISE TO OUR AFGHAN ALLIES IS STILL UNFINISHED FIVE YEARS LATER "We were just put in a very, very precarious situation that could have been better prepared for over the weeks and months prior leading up to that," Vargas-Andrews recalled. "And that decision was never made." Vargas-Andrews said troops had received intelligence warning of a threat, but maintained that nothing was done proactively to prevent it. He did not place responsibility on any single person or group, instead pointing to multiple administrations, the State Department and other organizations and citing "decades of action and inaction and just poor decision-making." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Vargas-Andrews welcomed the recent recognition by the Department of War of Marines who served during the evacuation, but said he did not want these awards to overshadow the fact that there has still been no accountability. "It's a good step in the right direction, is what I will say. I think that the real important things still haven't happened, but we hope it does and we pray that it does.," Vargas-Andrews said.

articles.title: Ahead of SCO, Uzbekistan joins India in condemning cross-border terrorism
articles.summary: India News: As the 2 countries elevated their relationship, Uzbekistan joined India in unequivocally condemning terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in al.
articles.body: As the 2 countries elevated their relationship, Uzbekistan joined India in unequivocally condemning terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, reiterated zero tolerance approach to terrorism and rejected justification of terrorism on any ground whatsoever in a joint statement.Even though the 2 countries share strong counter-terrorism cooperation, this formulation is significant as Uzbekistan has not used the specific phrase "cross-border terrorism" in the past apex-level joint statements (between PM and president), like those issued after summit meetings in 2015, 2018 and in 2020. According to official sources, this reflects stronger diplomatic alignment on state-sponsored terrorism and regional security dynamics, especially in the context of the SCO summit on Tuesday in which leaders will address issues like the need for stronger counter-terrorism and the Afghanistan situation."Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and for disrupting terrorism financing networks, safe havens and infrastructure. Leaders stressed that those responsible for terrorism should be held accountable and their perpetrators, their backers, facilitators and affiliates should be brought to justice," said the joint statement. The strongest wording so far had come in the 2020 joint statement, after a virtual summit, in which PM Narendra Modi and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and also underlined the need for every country to ensure that its territory is not used to launch terrorist attacks against other countries.Read more: India, Uzbekistan target long-term uranium pactOn this occasion, the leaders stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation in law enforcement, intelligence-sharing, and combating violent extremism, and illicit drug trafficking, organized crime, and cyber threats. They also reaffirmed the importance of continued cooperation under the Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism in the joint statement.India and Uzbekistan, which shares border with Afghanistan, have shared concerns about radicalisation and influx of militant groups. For India, it's important to work with Uzbekistan and other countries in the region to prevent Afghanistan from turning into a haven for terrorist groups, particularly like LeT and JeM based in Pakistan. Tashkent is also home to Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), a permanent SCO body responsible for coordinating efforts by member-states against terrorism, extremism and separatism."The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), recognizing it as an important platform for enhancing mutual trust, promoting regional peace, security and stability, and expanding cooperation in trade and economic affairs, investment, and cultural and humanitarian exchanges," said the joint statement.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Billions in US aid to Ukraine under microscope as corruption rocks Zelenskyy’s inner circle
articles.summary: Over 24 federal agencies oversee billions in U.S. defense aid to Ukraine as Zelenskyy dismisses officials amid widening anti-corruption probes, expert says.
articles.body: Washington is relying on extensive safeguards and dozens of oversight agencies to scrutinize and protect billions of dollars in U.S. aid to Ukraine amid the country’s continuing struggle with corruption, a regional security expert said Sunday. The oversight comes as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s inner circle faces renewed political pressure from widening investigations, with several senior officials and aides resigning, being dismissed or facing investigations since 2025. Zelenskyy dismissed Iryna Mudra, a deputy head of the presidential office, on Aug. 19 as anti-corruption investigators pursued a money-laundering case involving another deputy head of the office. Investigators have not named Mudra as a suspect, The Associated Press reported. ZELENSKYY SAYS PUTIN 'LOST THE INITIATIVE' AS UKRAINE'S TECH INDUSTRY RESHAPES THE WAR "Of course, in all of the former Soviet Union countries, there is significant corruption," former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Carrie Filipetti, now executive director of the Vandenberg Coalition, told Fox News Digital. "A lot more work needs to be done. But we know, at least on the U.S. side, as we're providing support for their military, we have a lot of mechanisms," she said before explaining how dozens of agencies are working on oversight of U.S. aid to Ukraine. The U.S. committed $67.8 billion in defense articles and services to Ukraine from February 2022 through March 2026 through the Presidential Drawdown Authority, the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative and Foreign Military Financing, congressional reports show. That support is part of a broader U.S. response to the war. About $195 billion has been appropriated for Operation Atlantic Resolve, including funds to replenish U.S. weapons stocks, support U.S. military operations in Europe and provide economic, development and humanitarian assistance, according to the Council on Foreign Relations. AS TRUMP'S NATO GAMBLE PAYS OFF, ENVOY NAMES ALLIES HE'S STILL WATCHING "Over 24 federal agencies are involved in oversight," Filipetti said. "To make certain that there are no consequences to the U.S. taxpayer, to our equipment in terms of the corruption issue, U.S. contributions are very much protected." In recent months, however, senior Ukrainian officials have resigned, been dismissed or faced scrutiny by the country’s independent anti-corruption bodies, including NABU. Those developments include Andriy Yermak’s Nov. 28, 2025, resignation after investigators searched his premises and Mudra’s Aug. 19 dismissal during a money-laundering probe. Former Deputy Prime Minister Olha Stefanishyna was dismissed by Zelenskyy as Ukraine’s ambassador to the U.S. on Aug. 3, two days before a suspicion notice was served against her, according to the Kyiv Post. He also fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov on July 15 in a broader reshuffle over internal wartime disagreements which sparked protests across the nation. ZELENSKYY PRESSURES US AND EUROPE FOR MORE 'AIR DEFENSE' ASSISTANCE AMID ONGOING WAR WITH RUSSIA In interviews after he left government, Fedorov also complained about what he described as ingrained corruption and patronage networks, Reuters reported. "We've seen that Zelenskyy is taking really seriously the criticisms of corruption, and every time there is an allegation, he moves very swiftly to remove those individuals from the government," Filipetti said. "And the fact that there are these independent bodies is, I think, really important. They're listening to them. They're making sure that they're trying to root it out as much as humanly possible." THE TWO MOST IMPORTANT AMERICAN WEAPONS SYSTEMS NATO IS EAGER TO HAVE Zelenskyy has pushed back on suggestions that the investigations implicate him personally. "The heads of anti-corruption agencies have zero questions for me," Zelenskyy said in remarks published Aug. 23 regarding the investigations. "They understand perfectly well that I am not involved in anything like that." A February 2024 USAID inspector general review also found that the agency did not independently verify some Ukrainian health workers’ salary claims before reimbursement, though Filipetti said U.S. economic aid is now reimbursed only after verification. "A lot of what the United States has been providing, we're making sure that everything is through a reimbursement mechanism," Filipetti said. TOP UKRAINIAN OFFICIALS IN ZELENSKYY GOVERNMENT SUBMIT RESIGNATIONS AMID $100 MILLION CORRUPTION SCANDAL She said U.S. aid has not been tied to the money-laundering allegations and remains protected as Ukraine works to combat corruption. The scrutiny also comes as Kyiv faces shortages of Patriot interceptors amid intensified Russian strikes and a need for air defense interceptors. Zelenskyy said he wants to secure 300 additional interceptors for the coming winter, while Ukraine’s air force has requested 360. "One of the most urgent needs that the Ukrainians have right now is interceptor missiles," Filipetti said. "This is why this idea of sending Patriot capabilities and allowing them to produce them on the ground in Ukraine has become so important to Zelenskyy." RUSSIA’S GAS GAMBLE BACKFIRES AS TRUMP’S ENERGY VISION RESHAPES EUROPE President Donald Trump has expressed reluctance to further deplete U.S. missile inventories, saying the United States also needs the weapons, while pressing European allies to shoulder more of Ukraine’s defense burden. "We want missiles too," Trump said Aug. 6 when asked about Zelenskyy’s requests for long-range missiles and Patriot systems. "Biden gave him so much, Biden gave $300 billion worth of ammunition." Filipetti also said Ukraine’s anti-corruption efforts remain an important consideration for its NATO aspirations. "I think every country has been really adamant that the Ukrainians move forward in their anti-corruption mechanisms," Filipetti said. articles.title: Dozens evacuated and about 15 missing after Grand Canyon flash flood
articles.summary: More than 60 people have been evacuated after flooding swept large boulders and other debris into the Colorado River.
articles.body:
At least 15 people are feared missing after major flash flooding hit the Grand Canyon in the US state of Arizona, the National Park Service has said.

As of Sunday morning, 62 people were evacuated due to flooding in the Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch areas on Saturday afternoon, the National Park Service said . The floods swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River, which runs through the park.

“The National Park Service is asking the public to provide information for approximately 15 individuals who may be missing or unaccounted for following a significant flash-flood event,” it said in a statement.

The flooding in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the Colorado River, wiped out footbridges over the creek and significantly altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and creating what appeared to be a new river rapid.

Popular tourist spots, including the Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch and parts of the North Kaibab trail, remained closed on Sunday while park officials surveyed the damage, the park said. Rafting trips on the Colorado River also have been halted for now.

Parth Desai was hiking through a narrow passage in Bright Angel Canyon with a group of fellow doctors and a park ranger when the downpour started.

“We saw the creek flood, waterfalls coming up out of nowhere; boulders, mud, landslides happening everywhere,” he told The Associated Press news agency.

“This is a reminder of what a dynamic and active landscape Grand Canyon is,” Jack Schmidt, director of the Center for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University, told AP.

The Grand Canyon National Park Service said it is working in coordination with the Arizona Department of Public Safety, with additional evacuations planned on Sunday. No injuries have been reported so far.

More rain and thunderstorms were forecast for the area into Monday.

articles.title: Sydney woman recalls how she punched shark during Coogee Beach attack
articles.summary: Leah Stewart, 34, was mauled by a great white shark in June during a morning swim at Coogee Beach.
articles.body:
A Sydney woman who survived a shark attack has described the moment she came face-to-face with a 4m great white before repeatedly punching it.

Leah Stewart, 34, was dragged under the water at Coogee Beach in June as the shark bit into her thigh and arms, leaving her with extreme blood loss and injuries so severe that doctors had to amputate her left arm.

In an interview which aired on Sunday, the mother-of-one said she was determined to live for the sake of her baby daughter.

"In my head, I was like, ... 'You are not taking me away from my daughter', and I twisted myself around and I just started punching it over and over and over again - it was like fighting a dinosaur".

Moments earlier, Stewart had just finished her regular Saturday morning swim and was heading back to shore when she was alerted to danger.

"I heard a girl behind me… a shrill shriek. I turned and there was a huge, huge fin behind her. It was massive," she told Nine Network's 60 Minutes.

"I looked at the size of it and I realised that's not a dolphin."

Stewart turned around and realised the shark was "right there … and it just was getting closer and closer and closer."

The shark's face was "horrific" with "black little beady eyes" and its "teeth and its mouth was massive".

"We were looking face-to-face," Stewart said, and at one point, the shark was just 30cm from her own.

Even in that moment, Stewart's thoughts remained calm.

"I'm right-handed, so I thought 'let's do a left hook'," she said.

"I just kind of throw my left arm and it just grabs onto my forearm and rips, rips away my skin, my muscle, everything... there's a big gap between my forearm and the hand."

The shark started to pull Stewart under the water, grabbing her leg.

"I had the thought, 'this is it, this is how I die' and then I just thought of [my daughter] August and I thought she's not going to have a mum, she's gonna grow up without a mum," she said, fighting back tears.

"I just knew I couldn't leave her... I know it sounds strange but I sort of willed myself back."

Fighting the shark felt "like punching a brick wall" but she kept going.

"I must have got a really good one in and so it let me go. It was the hardest thing in the world, but I fought my way out of there."

Stewart was pulled to the shore by other swimmers and rushed to hospital, where she was placed in an induced coma and underwent almost a dozen surgeries.

Despite her harrowing experience, Stewart said she doesn't want to be remembered as "a girl that got mauled on the beach".

"I'm the woman that punched the shark in the face," she said.

articles.title: Nicolás Maduro flashes peace signs in first prison photos since US capture in Caracas
articles.summary: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in his first photos from a New York prison, smiling as he awaits trial on federal drug trafficking charges.
articles.body: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in photos posted to his social media accounts Sunday, offering the first known glimpse of him inside a New York prison since his capture by U.S. forces in January. Maduro, who was flown to the U.S. following a major military operation in Caracas, has been in custody for eight months at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn while facing drug trafficking charges. In the photos, shared to Maduro’s X account, the former dictator wore a matching gray sweatsuit with white sneakers and appeared noticeably thinner as he stood against a plain wall. Maduro said he shared the images as a small gift of hope to his family and supporters, assuring them that "we will remain strong, serene, and confident" and that "Venezuela will be reborn." TRUMP TOUTS ACCESS TO 65 BILLION BARRELS OF VENEZUELAN OIL IN DEAL HE SAYS WILL SLASH GAS PRICES "I send these photos as a small gift to all my grandsons and granddaughters, to the boys and girls, and to all the noble people who love us," Maduro said. "I want you to know that we stand firm, with our hearts full of your love, that love that reaches us transformed into prayer, into constant action, into solidarity and true support. Infinite thanks for every word, for every gesture, for every blessing." "Enjoy this small gift with joy and hope. Cilia and I embrace you forever, with our souls devoted to you and with our faith in God intact," he added, referring to his wife, who was also flown to New York on related drug trafficking charges. MADURO ALLY DEPORTED TO US OVER ALLEGED BILLION-DOLLAR CORRUPTION SCHEME TIED TO OIL, FOOD PROGRAM While Maduro made the post Sunday morning, timestamps on the two photos indicate they were taken June 25, just one day after two major earthquakes killed more than 6,500 people in northern Venezuela near Caracas, according to The Associated Press. The images were released just two days after President Donald Trump announced a breakthrough in U.S.-Venezuela relations, with Venezuela agreeing to give the U.S. majority control over 65 billion barrels of oil from the nation’s reserves. The deal marks a major development for the American oil market as the ongoing war with Iran continues to push up prices at the pump. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Since being detained, Maduro has reportedly spent much of his time reading the Bible, according to his son, Nicolás Maduro Guerra, who spoke with El País in May. He added that the former leader has 510 minutes a month, or 8.5 hours, for conversations with people outside the prison, according to the report. Maduro and his wife are expected to go on trial in New York in June 2027. Both have pleaded not guilty and face potential life sentences if a jury finds them guilty of conspiring to send cocaine into the U.S.

articles.body: Microsoft is taking steps to reassure its workforce about the broader societal and environmental value of its computing infrastructure, even as artificial intelligence (AI) expansion complicates long-term climate targets. Citing an internal communication, Bloomberg says that Cloud Operations and Innovation head Noelle Walsh addressed growing staff inquiries regarding power consumption, water demands, carbon output and the direct footprints that these massive server campuses leave on nearby neighbourhoods.Walsh acknowledged that escalating AI workloads have made hitting earlier greenhouse gas reduction pledges considerably harder. However, she urged staff to consider ongoing engineering advancements, and that data centers must be built “with discipline, transparency and a relentless focus on reducing impact and increasing benefits,” she wrote.Internal unease at Microsoft mirrors broader public pushback against data centresThe internal message highlights how broader public scrutiny over AI infrastructure has reached the tech giant’s own ranks. Meanwhile, grassroots protests continue to centre on ecological strains, alongside wider fears that AI automation could eliminate jobs and disrupt local economies.Microsoft previously disclosed that its overall carbon emissions jumped 25% in 2025 due to rapid data facility construction. Consequently, the company has informed sustainability partners of plans to scale back new carbon-banking arrangements, while management has evaluated pausing an earlier goal to match 100% of its power consumption with renewable energy.Microsoft deploying efficiency upgradesWalsh pointed to significant technical progress designed to mitigate the environmental footprint of Microsoft’s infrastructure. Data centre water usage efficiency has improved by nearly 90% when compared against the firm’s earliest server facilities. The tech giant has secured commercial contracts to bring up to 40 gigawatts of renewable power online across global grids. Additionally, more than 90% of retired computer components and server hardware pulled from operational facilities are recycled or repurposed.To soothe tensions with municipal leaders and residents, major technology operators are overhauling their public outreach and offering significant concessions. articles.title: Urgent action needed to stop teachers quitting, says Liberal Democrats
articles.summary: A survey by the party suggested almost half of teachers reported considering quitting the classroom in the next five years.
articles.body:
Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.

Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.

The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.

The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".

The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.

Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.

More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.

Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.

The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.

"We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.

Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.

The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.

This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).

"After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.

"The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.

"That means fully funding the pay award and properly funding all our schools and colleges to stem the recruitment and retention crisis and give children the education they deserve."

"As Lucy Powell enters her first term as education secretary the Liberal Democrats are calling for her first act to be to introduce an emergency package of 'back to school' measures to face this crisis head on," Voaden said.

The Lib Dem proposals include the government fully funding teacher's pay, which will increase in England by 3.5% from September, with an additional 3% the year after.

Currently, half of the pay increase will come from existing school budgets.

The party is also calling for proper enforcement of teacher's legally mandated working hours, the introduction of reasonable limits on overtime, and for all schools to be required to introduce flexible working policies.

The party did not identify where funding might come from to pay for the policies.

An education department spokesperson said: "We know teachers do an incredible job and we're determined to make sure that dedication is matched with the right support.

"Last year saw one of the lowest rates of teachers leaving the profession since 2010, and a record number of teachers returning to the classroom, but we know there's more to do.

"We're taking action by announcing pay awards of almost 17% over two years, funding schools to improve maternity pay and offering targeted support to normalise flexible working and manageable workloads so that more teachers stay in our classrooms and thrive."

articles.title: Venezuela’s Maduro shares first photos from US detention
articles.summary: Abducted Venezuelan leader’s post appears to show him in US detention, published two days after US-Venezuela oil deal.
articles.body:
Former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro has posted two photographs that appear to show him in a United States detention centre, where he has been held since his January abduction.

US special forces abducted Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, from the Venezuelan capital, Caracas, and flew them to the US. The pair are being held in a facility in Brooklyn, New York, on drug trafficking and firearm possession charges, which they deny.

“I am sending these photos as a small gift to all my grandchildren, to the boys and girls, and to all the good people who love us,” Maduro wrote in Spanish on the social media platforms X and Telegram .

“I want you to know that we are standing firm, with our hearts full of your love,” he added.

“We will remain strong, calm and confident: God is with us. God will provide. Venezuela will rise again.”

The two pictures, Maduro’s first photos from US detention, show him wearing a grey tracksuit and making peace signs with his hands. He appears to have lost considerable weight since his capture.

The posts were published on Sunday, but the timestamp on both pictures indicates they were taken on June 25, a day after twin deadly earthquakes killed more than 6,500 people and caused widespread destruction in northern Venezuela.

The AFP news agency said it had attempted to contact the detention centre to find out if the photos were authentic and had been authorised, but did not receive a response immediately.

The message was published two days after Maduro’s successor, interim President Delcy Rodriguez, announced a “historic” oil agreement allowing the US to operate oil fields in Venezuela.

Maduro does not have access to newspapers or the internet in prison, but he is allowed to speak by phone with his family and lawyers for approximately 300 minutes a month, with a maximum of 15 minutes per call, according to a source close to the former leader.

Maduro and his wife’s trial in the US is due to begin on 1 June 2027, a federal court in New York announced in late July.

articles.title: US plans to sanction another bank to keep economic pressure on Iran
articles.summary: Washington has recently stepped up efforts to economically pressure Tehran amid the deadlocked truce talks.
articles.body:
Washington plans to impose sanctions on another bank this week as it steps up its campaign to economically isolate Tehran amid the deadlocked truce talks, the US Treasury chief has said.

In an interview with The Associated Press news agency on Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declined to name the bank to be targeted by sanctions.

The announcement comes just days after Washington said it would cut off the United Arab Emirates’s operations of Basque Misr from the US financial system after accusing Egypt’s second-biggest bank of doing business with the Iranian government.

“This is going to be financial violence if we have to,” Bessent told AP on Sunday. “We are showing people that we know who you are, you know who you are, and this has got to stop.”

⁠In an interview with the Reuters news agency, Bessent said the next step may be cutting off an institution entirely from the dollar-based financial system.

“You’re going ⁠to see a lot ⁠more of these every week,” he said on Sunday, ahead of a Group of 20 finance leaders ⁠meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. “We’re starting with the banks, and we’re telling ⁠the banks it’s not OK ⁠to have Iranian money and to aid the regime.”

The US has stepped up efforts to economically pressure Tehran to submit to Washington’s demands, a campaign dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast”, amid the stalled truce talks between both parties.

Last week, the Treasury Department imposed new sanctions on nearly 60 individuals and entities that Washington accused of being part of networks helping Iran generate oil revenue, procure weapons and conduct cyber-operations.

Iran, however, has rejected the latest US sanctions, with Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs Ali Madanizadeh saying they will fail.

Violence in the conflict resumed on Sunday , the first time since late July, with Iran launching missiles at two US bases in Jordan following a US attack on Larak Island in southern Iran.

Bessent is preparing to host the meeting of the G20’s finance leaders, where he will huddle individually with his counterparts from the world’s major and developing economies to encourage cooperation against Iran.

The US Treasury chief also told AP that he would speak to his Chinese counterparts at the meeting and “all options are on the table” in terms of sanctioning Beijing for its continued trade with Tehran .

But he rejected the idea that the US was reluctant to confront China, calling it “a completely false narrative that the media picked up on”.

He insisted that Beijing and Washington agreed on the need to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon.

articles.title: Beloved Texas chiropractor, hiking group among those unaccounted for after Grand Canyon flash flood
articles.summary: Dr. John Giusti's wife said the Texas chiropractor and his hiking group are among those missing after a flash flood tore through the Grand Canyon.
articles.body: A Texas chiropractor and the hiking group he was with are among those reported missing or unaccounted for after a flash flood tore through a remote stretch of the Grand Canyon, according to a public plea from his wife. Dr. John Giusti, a chiropractor and father of three from Granbury, Texas, was hiking and camping in the canyon when floodwaters swept through Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area on Aug. 29, his wife said in an update shared by Whipple City Family Chiropractic. "Please pray for Dr. John’s safety," she wrote. The family’s update said Giusti’s hiking group is "among those currently reported missing and unaccounted for." It said National Park Service search-and-rescue teams were conducting ground sweeps and helicopter operations across the canyon floor. PARK VISITORS FACE FLOOD DANGER OUT WEST WHILE SEVERE STORMS RIP THROUGH NY, NJ His wife asked ChiroHabit’s community to keep "my husband, his hiking group, and our families" in their thoughts and prayers, adding that the family would share official updates as they are confirmed by park authorities. ARIZONA STATE STUDENT VANISHES DURING GRAND CANYON TRIP JUST DAYS BEFORE GRADUATION, FAMILY PLEADS FOR HELP "Dr. John is the heart of ChiroHabit, but above all, he is a deeply loved husband, father and pillar of our family," she wrote. Photos posted to Giusti’s ChiroHabit business page also show him in the Grand Canyon before the flooding began. GRAND CANYON MYSTERY ILLNESS REPORTEDLY TRIGGERS NPS INVESTIGATION AFTER RAFTERS REPORT ALARMING SYMPTOMS The National Park Service has not publicly identified the approximately 15 people it is working to locate or account for, and officials have not confirmed Giusti’s name. The agency is asking anyone who knows of hikers or backpackers who were in the Bright Angel Creek corridor on Aug. 29 or who had a campground reservation there to contact investigators. Giusti practiced chiropractic care for 19 years and was a partner at Whipple City Family Chiropractic in New York for eight years before moving to Granbury in 2020, according to his business biography. He and his wife, Janet, are raising three daughters in Texas. Outside of work, Giusti enjoys hiking, hunting, fishing, running and martial arts, his practice said. ARMY BLACK HAWKS AIRLIFT 200-PLUS STRANDED CAMPERS AS MISSOURI FLOODS TRIGGER MORE 350 RESCUES Separately, the National Park Service said Sunday evening that recovery operations had been completed for a 46-year-old man near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River. The Coconino County Medical Examiner’s Office was on scene. NPS did not identify the man, disclose a cause of death or say whether his recovery was connected to the search for people who remain unaccounted for after the flooding. The flash flood began at about 2:30 p.m. on Aug. 29, according to the National Park Service. As of Sunday morning, 62 people had been evacuated from Phantom Ranch and the lower North Kaibab Trail, and no injuries had been reported. Nearly all footbridges across Bright Angel Creek were destroyed, cutting off hiker access across the waterway. The flooding also forced the closure of Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the North Kaibab Trail to Phantom Ranch, Black Bridge, Silver Bridge and the Colorado River to river traffic. EXPERTS ZERO IN ON LIKELY CAUSE OF DEADLY NEPAL MUDSLIDE, WITH MORE THAN 1,400 MISSING Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs said her "heart is with the families and loved ones of every person unaccounted for after the flash flooding at the Grand Canyon." Hobbs said the Arizona Division of Emergency Management is coordinating with the National Park Service and Coconino County Emergency Management to support search and recovery efforts.
